list.name: namespace
list.label: Instance
list.description: The instance this board reads. Empty on purpose: the chart's templates/grafana-dashboard.yaml replaces this entry with a hidden constant naming the instance it installs, so every namespace="$namespace" selector reads that instance's series and no other. There is no instance picker: each instance ships its own copy of this board, in its own Grafana folder.

title: DeviceChain — Event Processing (DETECT + REACT)
description: Operations board for the DETECT + REACT event-processing pipeline: consumer lag, watermark lag, fan-out and detection throughput, REACT dispatch health, per-tenant state budget (rules, live keys, retained samples), snapshot cost, and JetStream stream fill. The engine gauges (backlog, lag, state sizes) are reported by the replica that holds the detection partition and read zero on a standby.

panels.title: Consumer lag (undelivered)
panels.description: Undelivered resolved events waiting on the DETECT durable consumer — the primary falling-behind signal.

panels.title: In-flight (delivered-unacked)
panels.description: Delivered-but-unacked messages (in-flight work; a peer's during a rolling-update overlap).

panels.title: Watermark lag
panels.description: Wall-clock minus the engine watermark at the last checkpoint.

panels.title: Rules active
panels.description: Detection rules loaded into the DETECT engine.

panels.title: Events applied /s
panels.description: Resolved events fed into the DETECT engine.

panels.title: Checkpoints /s
panels.description: Committed DETECT snapshot checkpoints.

panels.title: Consumer backlog
panels.description: The DETECT durable consumer's broker-reported backlog.

panels.title: Watermark lag
panels.description: How far behind wall-clock the engine's logical clock is.

panels.title: Fan-out throughput
panels.description: Fan-out breadth, published detections, and clock-fired (absence/duration/session) detections.

panels.title: Detections rejected before publish
panels.description: Detections dropped before publish, by bounded reason: backstop (the rule does not belong to the tenant it claims, so it is refused rather than published), orphan (the rule was removed before its detection was published) and marshal (the detection could not be serialized).

panels.title: Fan-out eval errors
panels.description: Leaf-predicate evaluation errors during fan-out (rule treated as non-match). Should be ~0.

panels.title: Version-drop safety gates
panels.description: Detections dropped at publish because the device left the rule's scope or its profile version has been superseded. A persistent rise hints at stale pending timers surviving a rolling update.

panels.title: Actions dispatched
panels.description: REACT actions handed to their sink, by action type (raiseAlarm / clearAlarm / sendCommand).

panels.title: Dispatch faults
panels.description: Recognized-but-inert actions, derived events whose rule was gone, events dropped after the redelivery cap, and connector actions shed at the source for being over a tenant's outbound egress quota on the timeline its telemetry reached the platform. Poison-dropped rising is a REACT-sink outage; egress-shed rising is a tenant over its outbound quota. Each shed is dead-lettered with reason shed within a budget (shed-lettered); past the budget it is counted and summarised once per tenant per minute (shed-unlettered). A clock fallback is a dispatch metered on broker or arrival time because it carried no trigger time, in REACT or in the connectors service: sustained, a catch-up can be shed as a flood again. The connectors clock-fallback series exists only when the optional outbound-connectors service is installed.

panels.title: Live keyed-state entries
panels.description: Total live window/timer state entries across all tenants (the per-tenant budget aggregate).

panels.title: Tenants over rule budget
panels.description: Tenants currently exceeding the per-tenant rule-count budget. The offender is in the warn log (no high-cardinality label).

panels.title: Tenants over live-key budget
panels.description: Tenants currently exceeding the per-tenant live-key budget.

panels.title: Tenants over retained-sample budget
panels.description: Tenants currently exceeding the per-tenant retained-sample budget (the per-sample records held by window-shaped rules). The offender is in the warn log (no high-cardinality label).

panels.title: Live keyed-state entries
panels.description: Growth here is the memory-footprint signal for the keyed streaming core.

panels.title: Retained samples and pending timers
panels.description: The other two memory axes. Retained samples are the per-sample records held by window-shaped rules across all tenants; a long-window rule on one busy device moves this and not live keys. Pending timers are the entries waiting in the timer heap; a long absence or session timeout under frequent reporting moves this and not the other two. Pending timers are instance-wide and have no per-tenant budget.

panels.title: Checkpoint cost
panels.description: Wall-clock cost of the last snapshot commit.

panels.title: Snapshot size
panels.description: Serialized size of the last DETECT snapshot payload.

panels.title: Restore cost (startup)
panels.description: Time to restore engine state from the snapshot store at startup.

panels.title: Stream fill (messages)
panels.description: Per-stream message count vs the configured ceiling. When a stream reaches its ceiling the oldest messages are evicted (the discard-old policy). 80% fill is where the JetStreamStreamNearFull alert fires, not where eviction starts. Writers separately stop accepting new messages when a consumer's unread backlog reaches 90% of what its stream can hold (see the unread backlog panel below).

panels.title: Stream fill (bytes)
panels.description: Per-stream on-disk bytes vs configured MaxBytes ceiling.

panels.title: Consumer unread backlog (share of stream capacity)
panels.description: Each of this service's consumers: messages it has not read (pending plus unacknowledged) over what its stream can hold. History already read does not count, unlike the fill panels. At 100% the stream discards messages the consumer has not read.

panels.title: Fence geometry: unresolved and mismatched (per interval)
panels.description: Manifest entries whose geometry could not be obtained (installed carrying an error, so a rule naming one is COUNTED rather than silently reading as outside), and documents that did not hash to the address they were requested under. Unresolved is often transient and repairs on the reconcile sweep. Mismatch is never transient — it means the wrong row was served, something re-encoded the document in transit, or the archive is corrupt. Counts per evaluation interval, since these should be zero.

panels.title: Geometry cache hit rate
panels.description: Share of compiled-geometry lookups served from cache. This is the economic case for manifest delivery: editing one fence of a hundred should re-fetch and re-compile ONE geometry, so a healthy rate sits very close to 1. A collapse means the cache is thrashing (see the vertex-occupancy panel) and every fence edit is paying the full cross-service read the design exists to avoid.

panels.title: Geometry cache occupancy (vertices)
panels.description: Vertices held against the cache's bound. The bound is counted in VERTICES rather than entries on purpose — a three-vertex box and a five-hundred-vertex polygon are one entry each and differ ~500x in what they cost to hold, so an entry count would mean something different for every mix of tenants. Sustained eviction (the panel beside it) alongside a falling hit rate is the thrash signature.

panels.title: Geometry cache evictions
panels.description: Compiled geometries evicted from the cache to stay within its vertex bound, per second. Sustained eviction alongside a falling hit rate is the thrash signature.

panels.title: Rule-health updates discarded
panels.description: Fire-count updates that will never be written, by reason (full, overflow, closed, write_failed, purged, shutdown). Detection is unaffected; the console's fire counts are short by this much.

panels.title: Rule-health backlog (pending rules)
panels.description: Distinct rules with fire-count updates not yet written. The age of the oldest one is in the panel beside it.

panels.title: Rule-health backlog (oldest pending)
panels.description: Age of the oldest fire-count update not yet written: how stale the console's fire counts may be.

panels.title: Rule-health write throughput
panels.description: Fire-count updates admitted from published detections, merged into an already-pending rule row (coalesced), and committed to the database. Written below admitted for long means a backlog; coalesced is the single-row writes avoided.

panels.title: Derived publish time share
panels.description: Share of the detection loop's wall time spent handing detections to the broker at a checkpoint (100% means fully saturated). The published rate is on the fan-out throughput panel.

panels.title: Rule-health write failures and contention
panels.description: Background batch writes (one tenant's transaction) that failed or timed out and were discarded, and admissions that had to wait for the writer to swap or settle a batch. Failures mean the console's fire counts fall short (see the discarded panel); contention is a constant-time wait, never a database call. Both should sit at zero.

panels.title: Rule-health write latency (p50 / p99)
panels.description: How long each background rule-health fire counter batch write (one tenant's transaction) took, as the 50th and 99th percentile over a 5 minute window. Failed writes are included. This is the background writer, not detection-loop time.

panels.title: Derived publish ack latency (p50 / p99)
panels.description: How long each published derived event waited for the broker to acknowledge it, as the 50th and 99th percentile over a 5 minute window. Positive outcomes only. It is not detection latency: a detection waits for its checkpoint before it is written.
